messages.subject: MSstats 3.7.3 is released
parts:
MSstats 3.7.3 is released on http://msstats.org/msstats-2/

  - BUG FIXES

     1. groupComparionPlots  function : occasional error, when assigning FCcutoff, is fixed. (Thanks, Cheng)

     2. dataProcess  function : error with normalization='quantile'  is fixed. (Thanks, Silvia)


  - NEW FEATURES

     1. ProgenesistoMSstatsFormat  function : required input for this function is changed.

     2. SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat  function : required input for this function and processing steps are changed.

     3. PDtoMSstatsFormat  : new function for converting Proteome Discoverer output to MSstats required format.

     - Please check MSstats user manual for v 3.7.3 about required input (output from processing tools) for converters.


Please let me know if you have any difficulty and bugs.

Happy new year!!

- Meena

messages.author: b3c6794838d616e7
messages.subject: Re: MSstats 3.7.3 is released
parts:
Hi Meena,

I looked into the manual regarding SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(). There it says:

"First, it uses only noloss from F.FrgLossType. If not, multiple measurements for each feature and run can be happend."

I don't think this is a smart way to go, because it means that in the likely case that the strongest fragment ion is generated by water-loos or ammonium-loss, MSstats will simply ignore it! One might might indeed like to make sure that not several fragment ions originating from the same y- or b-ion are selected for quantification (e.g. y7-noloss and y7-H20-loss), but that would require a different filter function.

A second observation:

Spectronaut considers replicate IDs only unique within sample groups (grouped according to conditions). I thought that MSstats requires a unique BioReplicate ID across all samples, otherwise it would interpret these replicates as technical replicates. Here is what I get when I convert Spectronaut data having two treatment groups, with 3 biological replicates per group:

The function reports all peptides to be unique in proteins...well, looking at the PG.ProteinAccessions column I would argue: Yes, technically they are, because Spectronaut reports a ;-separated  list of protein ACCs in this field. So the peptides are only unique after protein grouping. Is that really what you want? This would accordingly give you protein group inference in the end, not a protein inference.

Greetings,
Tobi
